Current lessons:
P1d01 [tao-1d] (active) **Breadth first: starts are cheap and decide a lot.** A 45 s start ranks almost as well as a 450 s one, and one 450 s run is no better than the best of ten 45 s runs. Among 521 long starts only two were clearly ahead of the rest. Make hundreds of short starts before spending on depth.
P1d02 [tao-1d] (active) **Do not cut early.** The rank at 800 or 12,800 cells predicts the final rank only roughly: the lineage that won was not the leader before the last stage, and a lineage ranked 7th of 20 became 2nd after refinement. Carry a wide set (at least 20 to 30 lineages) into the high-resolution stage.
P1d03 [tao-1d] (active) **Soft restarts move lineages; hard ones stall.** At 51,200 cells every restart with p0 >= 16 stayed where it was, while p0 = 4 and 8 dropped the score by more than 1e-3 on the lineages that responded. Not every lineage responds: of three strong ones, one did. So try the soft restart on many lineages, not on the best few.
P1d04 [tao-1d] (active) **Try soft restarts at every resolution (conjecture).** They were first used only at the last stage. Early numbers of a cold start suggest that p0 = 8 at 3,200 and 12,800 cells lifts mediocre starts more than hard restarts did. Test it on a few lineages against p0 = 16 before relying on it.
P1d05 [tao-1d] (active) **Chain restarts on the leader.** After a soft restart that worked, restarting again from the result with p0 in 2, 4, 8, 16 gained about 1e-4 each round, three rounds in a row.
P1d06 [tao-1d] (active) **More cells is not better by itself.** At equal time 51,200 cells beat 204,800. Go higher only when a lineage has stalled at 51,200, and give the larger size enough iterations per stage.
P1d07 [tao-1d] (active) **Costs.** One 1,200 s restart at 51,200 cells costs about USD 0.03; a hundred 45 s starts cost cents. Breadth at the soft-restart stage is cheap: thirty lineages, two settings, two repeats is about USD 4.
P1d08 [tao-1d] (active) **Stop a lineage** when two restart rounds in a row gain less than 1e-5, and move its budget to new starts.
P1d09 [tao-1d] (active) **Calibration.** Typical values at 12,800 cells are 1.456 to 1.460. The reference is near 1.45467. A lineage that will pass shows a drop of at least 1e-3 at its first soft restart at 51,200 cells.
P1d10 [tao-1d] (active) **Truth.** A float score is not a result. Round to integers and check exactly only for finalists, and claim only through the gate, with a reference read in the last 30 minutes.
G01 [general] (active) Breadth first: short starts are cheap and rank almost as well as long ones. Make many short starts before spending on depth.
G02 [general] (active) Do not cut early: the rank before the last resolution stage predicts the final rank only roughly. Carry a wide set (20 to 30 lineages) into the high-resolution stage.
G03 [general] (active) Soft restarts (small p0, such as 4 and 8) moved lineages at high resolution; hard restarts (p0 >= 16) mostly stalled. Not every lineage responds, so try soft restarts on many lineages.
G04 [general] (active) Soft restarts may also help at intermediate resolutions (conjecture): test against a harder setting on a few lineages before relying on it.
G05 [general] (active) Chain restarts on the leader: after a soft restart that worked, restart again from its result with p0 in 2..16.
G06 [general] (active) More cells is not better by itself: at equal time a moderate resolution beat a 4x larger one. Go higher only when a lineage has stalled, with enough iterations per stage.
G07 [general] (active) Breadth at the restart stage is cheap on Modal CPUs (about USD 0.03 per 20-minute 1-CPU job).
G08 [general] (active) Stop a lineage when two restart rounds in a row gain almost nothing, and move its budget to new starts.
G09 [general] (active) A float score is not a result: check exactly only for finalists, and claim only through the gate, with a reference read in the last 30 minutes.
